editorial:
Imagine you are driving through the quiet woods of northern Idaho and you run into the most dangerous people possible. That is exactly how things kick off here. You get a mix of characters who have no business being together: a young black man looking for a fresh start, a white nationalist who is a total loose cannon, and two vacationers who just happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. The vibe is very tense from the start, making you feel like something is about to snap at any second. It feels like a powder keg waiting for a spark, and the way these different worlds collide keeps you on the edge of your seat.

The acting is surprisingly raw, and the tension builds up in a way that makes the violent bursts feel real and shocking. While some parts of the story move a bit slow, the payoff is worth the wait. If you enjoy gritty stories about faith and forgiveness, you will really dig this.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a violent showdown that forces the characters to face their deepest hatreds. After a series of tense fights and arguments, the white nationalist finally meets a brutal end, showing that hate only leads to destruction. The young man finds a sense of peace and redemption, proving that faith can win over anger. It ends on a bittersweet note, leaving you to think about how random encounters can change your life forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty character studies and stories about redemption.
